## Outline

| Tool | What it is | When it's the right call |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | Agent in your terminal that can read/edit files and run code in any folder | Editing papers, auditing replication packages, multi-file refactors, working in Stata/Matlab/Julia |
| **Cursor** | A code editor (VS Code fork) with an LLM bolted in | If you live in an IDE and want inline completions + chat in the same window |
| **ChatGPT / Claude.ai (web)** | Chat in a browser; can do "code interpreter"-style work in a sandbox | One-off questions; quick scripts where uploading a file is faster than installing anything |
| **GitHub Copilot** | Autocomplete-as-you-type, plus a chat panel | Fast inline suggestions in VS Code or JetBrains; less useful for multi-file work |

## A pragmatic recommendation

- If you have **one quick code question** and your project isn't open: use
  Claude.ai or ChatGPT in a browser.
- If you want **inline autocomplete** while you type: use Copilot or Cursor.
- If you want the AI to **work on a real project of yours** — reading
  several files, making coordinated edits, running things, and reporting
  back — use Claude Code (or Cursor's agent mode, which is similar in
  spirit).

## What this guide does *not* claim

- That Claude Code is best at every task. It is the right default for the
  econ-research workflows on this site, not a universal winner.
- That you have to pick one. Most colleagues end up using two: one
  agentic tool (Claude Code or Cursor) and one chat tool (Claude.ai or
  ChatGPT) for quick questions away from the keyboard.
